claims.text: An ab initio multiscale framework coupling DFT phonon spectra and electronic band structures can independently predict lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicit electron-phonon and oxygen-defect scattering calculations will improve heat-transport prediction in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed framework will reduce prediction errors by 30–50% relative to Debye-based, defect-free models.
Approximately 1 wt.% oxygen represents a realistic defect concentration for the relevant experimental HfNbTaTiZr samples.
Phonon lifetimes and electronic scattering rates can be calculated separately using DFT Brillouin-zone integrations combined with Boltzmann transport or nonequilibrium Green's-function methods.
The predictions will apply from temperatures below 200 K through 1200 K.
Phonon heat transport is dominant below 200 K in HfNbTaTiZr.
Electronic heat transport becomes significant between 300 and 1200 K in HfNbTaTiZr.
The approach is applicable to HfNbTaTiZr samples containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen impurities modulate phonon lifetimes and electronic scattering rates in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicitly decoupling electronic and phononic transport avoids conflating their thermal-conductivity contributions.
Direct treatment of electron-phonon and defect scattering captures atomic-scale complexities affecting thermal transport.
Predicted lattice and electronic thermal conductivities will each agree with experimental values within ±25%.
Earlier Debye-temperature and elastic-property models have larger overall prediction errors than the proposed framework.
Traditional analytical and DFT-based approaches assume perfect, defect-free bulk crystals.
Traditional approaches do not separately resolve lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
The approach may be unreliable at oxygen concentrations much greater than 1 wt.% or at temperatures above 1200 K.
The approach may be unreliable far below 200 K.
Defect modeling and electron-phonon coupling limitations create uncertainty in the predicted scattering rates and accuracy improvement.
Deviation of either separated contribution by more than 25%, or an error reduction below 30% relative to traditional models, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions broadly claim validity below 200 K, whereas the boundary says the method may be unreliable far below 200 K without specifying a lower validated temperature, leaving the cryogenic applicability range internally ambiguous.
The sample is described as high-purity while simultaneously containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, a substantial impurity level; the intended meaning of high-purity is not clarified.
